summary.text: Rick Larsen is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for Washington's 2nd District, which he has represented since 2001. Before Congress he worked in public affairs for the Washington State Dental Association, in economic development at the Port of Everett, and on the Snohomish County Council. He is the ranking Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and says his 2026 campaign centers on affordability, transportation, veterans, the fentanyl crisis, and the environment.

paragraphs.text: Larsen was born in 1965 and raised in Arlington, Washington, where he attended public schools.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Pacific Lutheran University in 1983 and a master's degree in public affairs from the University of Minnesota in 1990.
He worked as director of public affairs for the Washington State Dental Association and then as an economic development official with the Port of Everett.
Larsen served on the Snohomish County Council before running for Congress; Wikipedia lists his service as January 1998 to January 2001.
He won election to the U.S. House on November 7, 2000, defeating Republican John Koster and two minor-party candidates, and has been re-elected to 12 further terms.

He served as the lead Democrat (ranking member) on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee's Aviation Subcommittee from 2013 to 2022, and House Democrats elected him ranking member of the full committee for the 118th Congress, a post he still holds.

His 2025-2026 committee assignments are the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and its Aviation, Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation, Highways and Transit, Water Resources and Environment, and other subcommittees.

His official site lists him as a member of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly, co-chair of the bipartisan U.S.-China Working Group, co-chair of the Congressional Arctic Working Group and Congressional Austria Caucus, and member of the New Democrat Coalition and its Trade Task Force.
According to his official biography, Larsen lives in Everett with his spouse, Tiia Karlén; they have two sons.
